column1: # Known bugs of upstream versions and known differences between them, for
# scripts/interop.sh.
# Adapters are published on the latest upstream release even when it has a
# bug; the bug is listed here (and in docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) instead of
# pinning an older release or hiding it.
# Columns, separated by tabs:
#   1  implementation (adapter name) that has the bug
#   2  its upstream version, as print-capabilities reports it
#   3  the role the bug is in: edge or host
#   4  peer: regular expression on the adapter of the other role
#   5  broker: regular expression on the broker name
#   6  fixture: regular expression on the fixture name
#   7  step: regular expression on the step name: births, update-N, write,
#      rebirth-command, device-death, device-birth, rebirth-call, nodes,
#      graceful-death, will, primary-host-offline
#   8  what is wrong (docs/COMPATIBILITY.md has the details)
#   9  evidence URL pinned to the upstream version; the waiver in results.json
# Expressions match the whole name. In a pairing where the adapter of that
# role is that implementation at that version and columns 4 to 7 match, the
# step may fail and is counted as a known bug rather than as a failure. If it
# passes in every pairing that ran it, the run fails: the entry is stale.
# An entry whose description starts with "Specification ambiguity:" is a known
# difference between stacks that each read the specification validly, not a bug
# of the stack in column 1; it is held to the same rule.
# Entries that need a particular peer or broker are only checked for
# staleness in runs that include them. An entry whose description starts with
# "Intermittent:" is never stale: the bug shows only in some runs.
implementation
pysparkplug
column8: EdgeNode advances bdSeq again after NBIRTH, so the NDEATH of disconnect() carries bdSeq+1 and hosts keep the node online (tck-id-payloads-ndeath-bdseq)

column1: pysparkplug
column8: Specification ambiguity: decodes Int8 and Int16 only in the width-sized form, and a negative value sign-extended to 32 bits (as Tahu, tahu-js and SparkplugNet encode it) raises OverflowError and the whole NBIRTH is dropped

column1: pysparkplug
column8: Cannot decode a metric without a datatype, such as the bdSeq metric of srad's NDEATH and will, so the host keeps the node online (tck-id-payloads-metric-datatype-req)

column1: pysparkplug
column8: Cannot decode a command metric without a datatype (Sparkplug requires the datatype in births only): the edge node fails on an NCMD of srad or Tahu and disconnects (tck-id-payloads-metric-datatype-not-req)

column1: srad
column8: Intermittent: NanoMQ 0.25.7 publishes the will after an MQTT 5 DISCONNECT with reason 0 (srad's client speaks MQTT 5 only): a late NDEATH can take the restarted node offline ([MQTT-3.1.2-10], MQTT 5.0 3.1.2.5)

column1: pysparkplug
column8: Intermittent: applies the messages of an edge node in arrival order. MQTT orders messages per topic only, and NanoMQ and HiveMQ CE deliver messages of one node on different topics out of publishing order; the host takes the gap for a lost message, drops or misreads data, and requests a rebirth (MQTT 5.0 4.6; tck-id-operational-behavior-host-reordering-start)

column1: srad
column8: Intermittent: srad's AppEventLoop hands the messages of an edge node over in arrival order (its Resequencer serves generic_app only, which the adapter does not use), and the adapter's host checks seq in that order. MQTT orders messages per topic only, and NanoMQ and HiveMQ CE deliver messages of one node on different topics out of publishing order; the host takes the gap for a lost message, drops or misreads data, and requests a rebirth (MQTT 5.0 4.6; tck-id-operational-behavior-host-reordering-start)

column1: sparkplughost
column8: Intermittent: resequences the messages of an edge node by seq, but not across its NBIRTH. MQTT orders messages per topic only, and NanoMQ and HiveMQ CE deliver messages of one node on different topics out of publishing order; the host takes the gap for a lost message, drops or misreads data, and requests a rebirth (MQTT 5.0 4.6; tck-id-operational-behavior-host-reordering-start)

column1: tahu-js
column8: Cannot decode a command metric without a datatype (Sparkplug requires the datatype in births only, and srad and Tahu omit it): the value is null and the command is not applied (tck-id-payloads-metric-datatype-not-req)

column1: tahu-js
column8: Encodes UInt32 in long_value, where Sparkplug puts it in int_value (Google Protocol Buffer type uint32): srad rejects the metric, SparkplugNet reads 0 (Sparkplug 3.0.0 Datatype Details)

column1: sparkplugnet
column8: SparkplugNode filters the metrics of a DCMD against the node's metrics, not the device's, and resolves no aliases in commands (srad addresses them by alias): device writes and alias-addressed writes are dropped, so the data seq the hosts expect is off by one

column1: sparkplugnet
column8: SparkplugApplication updates its node and device states on NDEATH and DDEATH through a lazy iterator it never enumerates: dead nodes and devices stay online

column1: sparkplugnet
column8: Specification ambiguity: decodes Int8 and Int16 only sign-extended to 32 bits, and the width-sized form (pysparkplug, srad) throws OverflowException and the whole payload is dropped

column1: sparkplugnet
column8: Throws on a metric without a datatype (the bdSeq metric of srad's NDEATH and will) and drops the NDEATH, so the node stays online (tck-id-payloads-metric-datatype-req)

column1: sparkplugnet
column8: Sets seq in NCMD and DCMD, which Sparkplug forbids (tck-id-payloads-ncmd-seq): pysparkplug's edge raises TypeError on such a command

column1: tahu
column8: Encodes UInt32 in long_value, where Sparkplug puts it in int_value (Google Protocol Buffer type uint32): srad rejects the metric, SparkplugNet reads 0 (Sparkplug 3.0.0 Datatype Details)

column1: tahu
column8: On a DBIRTH after a DDEATH, TahuPayloadHandler keeps the device's old aliases, rejects the DBIRTH ("Not adding duplicated alias") and requests a rebirth (tck-id-payloads-alias-uniqueness)
